title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page completes the converse of the Weierstrass-type description built on the previous pages. Before this page, E is an elliptic curve over k with char k ≠ 2. F_∞ = ∪ F_n is the ring of rational functions regular outside the origin. Corollary 3 identified F_∞ ≅ k[P,P']/(P'^2 − (P^3 + a_1P^2 + a_2P + a_3)), with P ↦ ℘ and P' ↦ ℘'. The involution f ↦ f(−x) is P' ↦ −P'. The invariant derivation θ_δ is induced by θP = P', θP' = ½(3P^2 + 2a_1P + a_2). The normalisation is ℘'^2 = cubic with leading coefficient 1, hence the factor ½, available because char ≠ 2. The page finishes the preceding remark: in the bases F_n^± one can make explicit, in terms of a_1, a_2, a_3, both the multiplication law and the derivation θ_δ. Conversely, take a_1, a_2, a_3 ∈ k with Z^3 + a_1Z^2 + a_2Z + a_3 separable, i.e. discriminant Δ ≠ 0 (34). Then the same formulas define an elliptic curve E over k. It can be built as a projective completion of Spec F_∞; the notes say 'Proj(F_∞)', presumably the Proj of the Rees algebra of the filtration F_n. The map p = ℘ : E → P^1_k (35) factors through an isomorphism E/{±id_E} ≅ P^1_k. It is a double (quadratic) cover branched over the three roots z_i of the cubic (36) and over ∞. The origin of E lies over ∞. Finally, J = image of the nonzero 2-torsion ₂E* is the set of roots of the cubic. The inclusion J ⊂ P^1_k gives a canonical isomorphism (37) Σ_J ≅ P^1_k, sending a distinguished point t to ∞. Σ_J is presumably a canonical projective line attached to a 3-point (étale degree-3) scheme J, defined earlier in the notes. The purpose is to set up the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2 via the data (E, 2-torsion). The page is a standard textbook step: the Weierstrass equation y^2 = cubic, the double cover of P^1 branched at four points, and E/±1 ≅ P^1.
errors: Minor slip in the text: the cover is branched at all three roots z_i and at ∞ (four branch points), not 'at one of' the three points; the inserted 'l'un' seems to belong to a phrasing like 'en l'un quelconque des trois points … et en ∞'.
On the previous page, formula (33) should read θ_δ(℘') = ½(3℘^2 + 2a_1℘ + a_2), not ℘' = …; this is probably a transcription or notational slip.
'Proj(F_∞)' is loose: F_∞ is an ungraded ring. One must mean the Proj of the graded ring ⊕F_n (Rees algebra of the filtration), or the projective closure of Spec F_∞.

ideas.what: Converse: a separable cubic gives an elliptic curve y^2 = Z^3 + a_1Z^2 + a_2Z + a_3 (char ≠ 2) whenever Δ ≠ 0.
E → E/{±1} ≅ P^1 is a double cover branched at the images of the 2-torsion points, with the origin over ∞.
ideas.modern_name: hyperelliptic (Kummer) quotient of an elliptic curve; x-coordinate map

ideas.what: Canonical identification Σ_J ≅ P^1 attached to the 3-point set J = image of ₂E*, with t ↦ ∞.
ideas.modern_name: level-2 structure / Legendre-type normalisation; P^1 canonically attached to a degree-3 étale scheme (closest notion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre form); moduli-theoretic version in Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Weierstrass-model converse and the E/±1 ≅ P^1 double cover. The only mildly idiosyncratic element is the canonical Σ_J ≅ P^1 attached to the 2-torsion set, which is part of a coordinate-free set-up for moduli in characteristic ≠ 2. It is not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'Proj(\mathcal{F}_\alpha)' should be 'Proj(F_∞)' (F with index ∞, as in (31)); likewise 'où F_∞ est défini par (31)'.
The garbled passage reads roughly: '…), que [p est le] revêtement quadratique de P^1_k défini par (35)'; the struck word is perhaps 'quasi-multiplicatif' or similar.
In (35) the diagram is E → E/{±id_E} followed by an isomorphism (marked ≀) to P^1_k.
'ramifié en l'un des trois points z_i de P^1_k(k) = k solutions de l'équation (36)', presumably with ∞ also meant; the '=k' annotation refers to the affine part of P^1(k).
'unité de E étant au-dessus de la [section] ∞ de P^1_k' (the struck 'd'élément' precedes 'unité').
The last lines read 'l'inclusion J ⊂ P^1_k définit un iso canonique (37) Σ_J ≅ P^1_k, t ↦ ∞'.
